sanskrit: apādyaud apātatanad apaskandya vadhed ahim | kalyāṇyā yathā smitaṃ śam u naḥ santu vidyutaḥ ||
english: It sprang forth, it rushed off, it leapt aside and would strike the serpent — may the lightnings be propitious to us, even as an auspicious smile.

sanskrit: yat parjanya stanayati sarvaṃ saṃvijate jagat | patiṃ tad ṛtviyāvatī pṛthivī prati modate ||
english: When Parjanya thunders, the whole moving world trembles; the earth, ready at the proper season, rejoices facing her lord.

sanskrit: eṣa enā abhy akrandīd vṛṣāśvo dhenukā iva | ahīṃs tvaṃ vidyutā jahi māsmākaṃ puruṣān vadhīḥ ||
english: He has thundered upon her as a stallion-horsed bull upon a milk-cow — do thou, O lightning, smite the serpents; slay not our men.

sanskrit: abhikrandāt stanayitnor avasphūrjād aśanyā uta | devā maruto mṛḍata naḥ pātu no duritād avadyāt ||
english: From the roaring of the thunder, from the crackle of the thunderbolt — O gods, O Maruts, show mercy to us; may it guard us from peril and from disgrace.

sanskrit: ṛjīte pari ṇo nama- -ādityāḥ śarma yacchata | yuyuta parṇinaṃ śaram utāparṇaṃ riśādasaḥ ||
english: Bending away, bow around us — O Ādityās, grant us shelter; ward off the feathered arrow and the featherless one of Riśādas, the devourer.

sanskrit: kṛtavyadhani vidhya taṃ yaś cakāra tam ij jahi | na tvām acakruṣe vayaṃ vadhāya saṃ śiśīmahe ||
english: O kṛtavyadhanī, piercer of the fashioned wound — pierce him who made it; slay that very one. We do not whet thee for slaughter against one who has not acted against us.

sanskrit: yathā te devy oṣadhe pratīcīnaṃ phalaṃ kṛtam | evā tvaṃ kṛtvane kṛtyāṃ hastagṛhya parā ṇaya ||
english: Just as, O divine herb, thy fruit has been turned westward, so do thou seize the sorcery of the sorcerer by the hand and lead it away.

sanskrit: punaḥ kṛtyāṃ kṛtyākṛte godhevāvaṭam anv ayat | saktur iva saktupreṣyaṃ pratīcī prati dadhvasat ||
english: The sorcery goes back to the maker of sorcery, as a monitor lizard that has found its burrow; like flour dispatched to the flour-consumer — may it blaze back, turned westward.

sanskrit: yāṃ te cakrur vartaneṣu vārtākuṣu vṛtāsu ca | maṇḍūke kṛtyāṃ yāṃ cakrus tayā kṛtyākṛto jahi ||
english: The sorcery they wrought upon the roads, upon the eggplants, and in the circular enclosures, and the sorcery they worked into the frog — with that very (sorcery), slay the sorcerer.

sanskrit: agnir ivaitu pratikūlam anukūlam ivodakam | sukhe ratha iva vartatāṃ kṛtyā kṛtyākṛtaṃ kṛtā ||
english: May it advance against (its maker) as fire (advances) against the wind, as water (flows) with the current; may the sorcery, once fashioned, turn upon the sorcerer who fashioned it, as a chariot turns upon a smooth road.

sanskrit: agnir dyumnena sūryo jyotiṣā dyaur mahimnāntarikṣaṃ vyacasā | diśa āśābhiḥ pṛthivī payobhir idaṃ rāṣṭraṃ vardhayantu prajāvat ||
english: Agni with his brilliance, Sūrya with his light, Dyaus with his greatness, the atmosphere with its expanse, the directions with their prospects, the earth with her waters — may they cause this kingdom to flourish, rich in offspring.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭā rūpeṇa savitā savena- -ahar mitreṇa varuṇena rātrī | pūṣā puṣṭair bhago aṃśena bhaktyā- -idaṃ rāṣṭraṃ vardhayantu prajāvat ||
english: Tvaṣṭṛ with form, Savitṛ with his impulsion, Day with Mitra, Night with Varuṇa, Pūṣan with nourishments, Bhaga with his share and apportionment — may they cause this kingdom to flourish, rich in offspring.

sanskrit: yāṃ viśvakarmā nijaghāna methim antarā dyāvāpṛthivī ubhe | tasyā āhuḥ kṣatriyaṃ garbham etaṃ pari māva patthā mūrdhani dhārayasva ||
english: The peg that Viśvakarman drove between the two — Heaven and Earth — of that (peg) they call this kṣatriya the offspring; do not fall away from it; bear it upon thy head.

sanskrit: chandāṃsy asyā abhito mayūkhā stomā ātmā yajur asyāḥ purīṣam | tasyā āhuḥ kṣatriyaṃ nirmitaṃ pari māva patthā mūrdhani dhārayasva ||
english: The metres are its rays on every side, the stomas are its self, the yajus is its substance — of that (sovereignty) they call the kṣatriya fashioned; do not fall away from it; bear it upon thy head.

sanskrit: parā ṇudasva vyathayābhimātim adhaspadaṃ kṛṇuṣva durdharāyataḥ | mā tvā dabhan sapatnā dipsantas tava rāṣṭram uttamaṃ dyumnam astu ||
english: Push away the affliction with confusion; crush the intractable adversary down underfoot; let not rivals, seeking to deceive thee, delude thee — may thy kingdom be of the highest splendor.
